events.title: LAG_X, the MSX2's view lag in x for D3 (docs/PERF2_PLAN.md D3, the user's choice, default 32): with the V9938 engine the view shown may lag LAG_X pixels (32-64) behind the camera in x before the cadence holds the ticks. msx/player.asm cam_lag: after cl_abs's test of LAG_MAX (32, as always), a lag of 32 or more in x holds the ticks only up to LAG_X when fb_eng is 1 (the V9938's two pages: an MSX2, or FORCE_V9938); the V9958's ring (fb_eng 0: the MSX2+ and the turbo R) returns as before, so their cadence decides as without the option. y keeps 32; rc_safe keeps RoboCop at least 16 pixels from the screen's sides (unchanged); D = 0 on the hold as the cadence needs (LAG_X - 32 below 256). From C/a_loop/lagx64.diff (x 64, y 32), which relaxed x on every machine: here the V9938 engine only. 12 bytes of the fixed area, none without the option. tools/mkrom.py: the option (32-64). tests/test_cadence_options.py: the option and its refusals, its code in player.asm only, its rule from the code (held from 64 px with the V9938 engine, from 32 with the V9958's, from 32 without the option). README.md's options row, docs/MSX_ARCHITECTURE.md "Game logic". Checked: the 14 builds without the option byte-identical to a431d23's; the LAG_X=64 builds, 14, with the 12 known warnings; the code bytes read back from its product.

events.title: CAD_ADAPT, the cadence's option for D2's loop-3 (docs/PERF2_PLAN.md D2, the user's choice, default 0): a picture that took fewer than CAD_ADAPT VBLANKs runs at most 2 game ticks, only a slower one up to CAD_MAX or CAD_HOLD. Loop-3 is CAD_MAX=3 CAD_HOLD=3 CAD_ADAPT=8 (3 ticks a picture only below 7.5 pictures a second at 60 Hz; the faster scenes as today); loop-1 is CAD_MAX=3 CAD_HOLD=3 alone, the options C/a_loop's analyst measured loop-1 with (its c3 builds and T_c3 trace builds: CAD_MAX 3, CAD_HOLD 3). msx/player.asm cadence: at cd_cap, with wf_n below CAD_ADAPT, a cap of 3 or more becomes 2 (C/a_loop/ad3.diff's rule; a cap of 0 or 2 stays): 14 bytes of the fixed area, none without the option. tools/mkrom.py: the option (0-255; refused with CAD_MAX and CAD_HOLD both 2, where it would do nothing). tests/test_cadence_options.py: the option and its refusals, its code in player.asm only, its rule from the code (2 ticks below 8 VBLANKs, 3 from 8 on; caps 0 and 2 untouched). README.md's options row, docs/MSX_ARCHITECTURE.md "Game logic". Checked: the 14 builds without the option (product, drive, trace) byte-identical to a431d23's; the loop-3 and loop-1 builds, 14 each, build with the 12 known warnings; the code bytes read back from the loop-3 product.

events.title: FLASH_LOOK 7 counted in game ticks (docs/PERF2_PLAN.md D1, still the user's choice, default 0): an enemy is white in the tick of a hit and the 3 ticks after it, and every hit starts the 4 ticks again, so hits at most 4 ticks apart keep it white. The first 7 counted pictures (white in the hit's picture and the next one); on the turbo R, at about 1.5 ticks a picture, Cain's hits came 3-4 pictures apart and the hold lapsed (58 look changes on the ground floor). msx/bob.asm: bob_begin, at every game tick's start (its one caller is player.asm gt_go), shifts each slot's fl_pend byte right; fl_note sets bits 0-3 (0Fh) and returns BM_FLASH, fl_held returns bit 0; no held-hit bit and no bob_skip test for 7: a hit in a skipped tick is still inside its 4 ticks at the tick shown for a frame of up to 4 ticks (tools/mkrom.py refuses FLASH_LOOK=7 with CAD_MAX or CAD_HOLD above 4). msx/rc2.asm's frame end builds no fl_pend loop for 7 (ml_tkd stays as the label). FLASH_LOOK 6 is unchanged (its own block, the same bytes). OS_FLASH, the results and everything the logic reads as always. Free bytes: the fixed area 22 more with 7 than without the option (product code_end 7E1Dh -> 7E07h; the first 7 cost 2), LC1 5 fewer (slot_clear, as before). tests/test_flash_look.py: 7's rule from the code (fl_note's store, fl_held's mask, bob_begin's shift; 4 white ticks for a hit, restarts, steady at hits 4 ticks apart, the pictures at 1-4 ticks a picture, a hit in a skipped tick never lost), bob_begin's one caller, no frame-end loop and no held hit for 7, mkrom's refusal; 6's rule as before. tools/mkrom.py's help, README.md's options row, docs/MSX_ARCHITECTURE.md "The hit flash's look" (the measured numbers of the first 7 marked as such). Checked: every build without the option byte-identical to a431d23's (the product, the 13 drive and trace builds of gate.sh builds); FLASH_LOOK 6's 14 builds byte-identical to a431d23's with FLASH_LOOK=6; 7's code bytes read back from the product ROM; tests/test_flash_look.py 7 passed, and fails with fl_note storing 07h or fl_held masking bit 1.

events.title: Level 3's beams and turrets write their looks with the tiles looked up at build time (performance campaign 2, logic-2): tools/mapcells.py look_tables writes each map word of lt2_top, lt2_left, lt2_right, the off words, tur_panel, tur40_look and tur41_look as its tile (the level's OTILE at the word >> 7) and its attributes, 3 bytes a word, into gen/tt_l3.inc and tt_l3b.inc at every build (tools/mkrom.py); msx/level3.asm lt2_putt and msx/level3obj.asm tpu_w call the new msx/tiles.asm map_write_t (map_write after its lookup and its two bank switches) instead of map_write_lin, their columns 18-63 never needing its wrap (tools/mapcells.py fails the build otherwise); tiles.asm rd_bit finds a cell's bit without loops (the same byte and bit for every row and column 0-159). tests/test_level3_logic.py: the tables equal map_write's lookup of the original words (synthetic and level 3's own), the writers' columns, the beam records against BM_N, rd_bit's index exhaustively. docs/MSX_ARCHITECTURE.md (with both items' measured speeds) and docs/LEVEL3.md 3.3. Checked: make test with the 4 known failures only (356 tests); 58 of the 61 option sets build (the three DEMO sets fail as before); the logic traces against the bench 0 differ (level 3's 16, level 2's 23, level 1's cov1, cov0, cov0_tr) with the lost counters 0; the map's state equal to the base's every 100 ticks (tour3, park; C-BIOS_MSX2, FS-A1FX). events.title: FLASH_LOOK (tools/mkrom.py): the hit flash's look, for the user's choice (docs/PERF2_PLAN.md D1; nothing decided, every build without it byte-identical: the 58 variant sets that build, the drive, trace and product builds). 6 = at most one white picture in 4 per enemy; 7 = an enemy stays white while hit less than 2 pictures apart and turns normal 2 pictures after its last hit. msx/bob.asm fl_note, fl_held and fl_due decide only the BOB record's look (bob_mode) per enemy slot and picture shown; OS_FLASH, the results and everything the logic reads as always. fl_pend's byte per slot keeps the held hit in bit 0 and the look's pictures to come in bits 1-4, shifted right at rc2.asm's frame end (ml_flc); a hit arms from bit 2 up, so every part of an enemy takes one look; objects.asm slot_clear clears the byte for a new enemy. No RAM of its own. Free bytes: the fixed area 164 -> 158 (6) or 162 (7) in the product, 100-119 -> 94-113 or 98-117 in the drive and trace builds; LC1 24 -> 19 (153 -> 148 in the level-1 trace build); the other banks unchanged. tests/test_flash_look.py (the option, where its code is, the rule from the code's constants); docs/MSX_ARCHITECTURE.md "The hit flash's look" (what changes per level, the measured speeds and looks); README.md's options. Checked: the logic traces with FLASH_LOOK 6 and 7 (level 3's 16, level 2's 23, level 1's cov1, cov0, cov0_tr) 0 differ, lost counters 0; the look's rule without an exception on kill, boss and l2_barrel on the MSX2, MSX2+ and turbo R; make test the 4 known failures only.

events.title: Level 3's map-write caches (performance campaign 2, logic-1): a beam in its off phase (msx/level3.asm lt2_off) and a wall turret's panel and turret blocks (msx/level3obj.asm tur_put) no longer write the words their cells hold. Every map change counts in mw_gen (msx/tiles.asm atr_put's change path and fb_invf; msx/cold.asm tiles_init); each writer keeps an entry (per beam record bm_gen; per turret type and block the look, the cell and mw_gen) that stands only in the tick after its own use (mc_cur and mc_prev, aged by msx/special.asm hz_update at every tick's start, cleared by l3_init at every life) and only while mp_lost and atr_lost are 0, so a skipped write is one that would have changed nothing. tiles.asm cam_cells takes the cells with add hl,hl four times (the same B and C for every value). events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Kilrathi Saga reconstruction now models Win32 shell byte views separately from the game modules’ integer flags and names more globals from DOS source while retaining an upstream-reported exact 518,656-byte executable match.
change_details.after: Kilrathi Saga reconstruction and SDL2 port now runs the Super Wing Commander demo from MacBinary copies, decodes resource/data forks and AIFF sample variants, and restores demo option, volume and starfield behavior; exact-match work for the Windows executable remains separately bounded.

after: Super Wing Commander demo resource playback

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: PAL 2.00 PS2 reconstruction now shares typed LevelState/camera, render, pause, particle, puzzle and memory-card structures across overlays; these structural refactors do not by themselves establish additional matching or playability.
change_details.after: PAL 2.00 PS2 reconstruction now replaces thousands of stale shared extern declarations with per-file headers through a checked migration tool; this structural cleanup does not by itself establish additional matching or playability.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Active browser and Electron emulator with debugger, rewind, media inspection and automated CPU tests; not independently built or run in this review.
change_details.after: Active browser and Electron emulator whose debugger now supports reverse-continue to a previous breakpoint or watchpoint, reverse step-out and last-writer lookup; upstream released these changes in 2.18.0, but the tracker did not independently run them.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Firestaff now verifies an accepted original-asset Macintosh viewport/HUD frame before the DM2 launcher returns, while distinguishing a French-named archive from evidence of a localized French runtime; broader native playability and Nexus completion remain open.
change_details.after: Firestaff now adds a native Apple IIGS melee-action path and parses Macintosh sound and SONG resources while refining authenticated-media candidate reporting; broader native playability and Dungeon Master Nexus completion remain open.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Source inspected; no independent build or execution
change_details.after: GameCube reconstruction now uses Ghidra/REA-backed drafting, variant search, m2c drafts, finishable-unit ranking and stricter gap workflows while matching additional PS2DMA packet helpers; no independent build or execution was performed.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Active alpha native reconstruction; CD-i port in progress; upstream-playable ports remain close rather than exact
change_details.after: Active native C reconstruction and console-port project; upstream added a proof-of-concept NABU network version and removed CD-i from the supported-platform list, so CD-i is no longer presented as an active supported port.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.after: Independent DOS analysis and SDL port now refines town-shop NPC timing, cavern message-box/draw ordering and background/status rendering against original binary oracles; the tracker did not independently run the comparison scenarios.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Amiga-source-derived SDL2 PC/web port; its editor now assembles complete original-map room graphics streams and preserves packed point-lighting animation controls, while new-geometry authoring and playable newly drawn rooms remain unproven.
change_details.after: Amiga-source-derived SDL2 PC/web port whose editor now supports safer shared-corner editing, discoverable texture painting, native textured FPS editing and floor-material banks while preserving editor camera state across playtests; newly authored full levels remain unproven.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: MAIN message functions now use standard varargs while the full 518,656-byte executable and mandatory hash remain exact; two instruction-value checks cover 1,550 functions, with documented declaration and qualifier blockers still open.
change_details.after: Kilrathi Saga reconstruction now models Win32 shell byte views separately from the game modules’ integer flags and names more globals from DOS source while retaining an upstream-reported exact 518,656-byte executable match.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: The preserved 1995 DOS source now ships playable Linux, Windows x64, macOS and web ports plus a compatible level editor; differential fuzzing also corrected the documented same-turn arrow/glass rule.
change_details.after: The preserved 1995 DOS source and modern ports now include mkpit, which compiles bounded text maps, legends and scripts into compatible PIT level files; playable-port status is unchanged.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Active PS1 emulator/debugger now models CD-ROM pickup, spin-up, Init, Pause and GetID timing from SCPH-7001/9002 measurements and applies NTSC 480i DFE row suppression in both software and OpenGL GPU paths; independently unbuilt and unrun.
change_details.after: PCSX-Redux now clears GPUSTAT bit 26 throughout incomplete multi-word GP0 commands and GP0(C0h) readout until the final word, matching an added silicon-focused regression test; independently unbuilt and unrun.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Moria8 adds disk save/load playtests, retry paths and deterministic failed-run capture across its 6502/65C02 ports; released/platform status is unchanged and tracker-side execution was not performed.
change_details.after: Moria8 now treats truncated Commodore drive-status reads as lost, retries only probes that can issue a fresh OPEN, and fails ambiguous save status rather than reporting success; upstream playtest-disk scenarios pass across C64, Plus/4 and C128.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: The reconstruction now records three passing Xtensa firmware profiles with exact size budgets and an original-ROM oracle with 14/14 scalar STRING cases observed twice; device execution and broad BASIC compatibility remain explicitly unverified.
change_details.after: The reconstruction now has a host-verified bounded C99 ESC/ANSI transport contract with malformed-CSI quarantine; original CPC ESC behavior, BREAK on device and a native hardware run remain explicitly unverified.

before: three-profile Xtensa size and ABI verification
after: three-profile Xtensa size and ABI verification

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Source inspected; no independent build or execution
change_details.after: MDFourier now uses amplitude-spectrum scaling in sample units, reports amplitudes relative to the strongest tone, and derives the digital noise floor consistently in dBr; the tracker did not independently build or compare captures.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Amy Studio adds ten explicitly labelled faithful COMPUTE! adaptations as ColecoVision examples, preserving source-game rules and quirks while remaining an original browser development environment.
change_details.after: Amy Studio adds Shaker and Star Strike as explicitly non-port ColecoVision adaptations built from 1986 Ahoy! article rules, plus compiler support for inline VoxPCM and variable shifts; they remain original adaptations inside the browser development environment.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Amiga-source-derived SDL2 PC/web port; its new editor pipeline has transactional room-source history, validated portal topology and collision/corner-wall rebuilding from original LEVELSAVE contracts, but complete-file assembly and playable newly drawn rooms remain pending.
change_details.after: Amiga-source-derived SDL2 PC/web port; its editor now assembles complete original-map room graphics streams and preserves packed point-lighting animation controls, while new-geometry authoring and playable newly drawn rooms remain unproven.

events.title: docs/LEVEL3.md: level 3's plan. The original (REA on build/ram/level3_full.bin and the bench): the way in, the header $86B4 and level_init's level-3 part (no gun opening, state 6, the fade's state 0Bh), the map (50 rows, floors, 106 tiles in view), palette C identical to level 2's (mean dE76 2.18 against 2.68), the beams (level_tick_2: two cells, 32/32 frames, 0Ch), the three two-part lifts, the turrets' map writes, act_20, the 39 spawn entries and the markers (type 0 spawns nothing, type 43's markers_off), the 20 types with their handlers, sizes (4,222 B of level-3-only code), deaths and frames, Cain as RoboCop 2 (invulnerable above y 290h, the launch mailbox, his death and the level's end), the bullets and debris, the 202 frames drawn (58 of 48 px or more), the sound (nothing new), the end and the hand-over (level_load_3 $86DE), nine quirks. The design: the descriptor's third entry, the flow's hooks, two logic banks (BANK_L3, BANK_L3B behind a trampoline), the 2 MiB image's rules, the free bytes now, a dynamic frame cache in page 2 for Cain and type 21 with a white hit flash, a per-level FIELD_ID0, the pool in place, ENEMY_CAP's types, RAM homes, the VRAM map, the tools and the bench. The checks, five steps (A data, flow and bench; B logic and C play field side by side; D Cain, the end and the sound; E acceptance) and 15 defaults, the risks. docs/level3/HANDOFF.md: the log of the rest of the game, step 2's section. docs/AMIGA_ANALYSIS.md: level 3's ledger. docs/ROM_BUDGET.md 7: the level-3 image and coverage done

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Development head now recognizes NES inline dispatchers that save Y in absolute RAM and narrows conditional tail calls to genuine entries; bounded Punch-Out!! and SMB3 corpus results improve without treating ROM writes as harmless save noise.

events.title: Project metadata updated

events.title: Project metadata updated

events.title: Level 2's step 21, the code: CHEAT and the sound checks' tools. tools/mkrom.py CHEAT=1 (not with DIAG): cold.asm ng_init sets AG $804F FFh at each new game (the title's cheat handler $11F60: st.b $804F, REA), frame.asm fe_keys at frame_end's head maps F5 to key code 59h and F4 to 58h in $8032 while held, the code + 80h once let go (frame_end already acts on them: the original's F10/F9); there, in BANK_LC3, not in player.asm key_scan, so that the fixed area pays nothing (every set's code_end as before; LC3 -33 B, FRONT -5 B in CHEAT builds). sound.asm: label sf_back (no byte). New tools/bstest/fxlog.tcl: every PSG write (R0-R13), SCC write (9800h-98FFh, where it went) and OPLL write with the engine's events (requests queued, taken, ticks, stops, text screens, the stages' tune ticks), jobs fxl_jobs (level 2's drives tour, vat, mine, end, t1left, trolley on the cartridge's SCC, an SCC in slot B and the PSG alone; the continue; the briefings; both stages' visits); hz.sh fxbuilds. New tools/bstest/fxcheck.py: a model of sndplay.asm and music.asm's in-game effects replays every event from the logged state and compares each segment's writes, the queue's order, the tick divider, the end state, per effect its starts, refusals and plays to the end, the bench's requests per frame, the text screens' silence; visits (the stages' tunes tick for tick), selftest (mutations). New tools/bstest/cheat.tcl: a CHEAT=1 build by the keyboard from the power-on through both levels. variants.sh: the 5 CHEAT sets (53). Tests: tests/test_fxcheck.py (15), test_level2_rom.py CheatTests, test_bstest.py's count.

The plan's mechanism, rd_at's base in pz_tvb, was built first and rejected: its 113 T more at visit 1's entry moved visit 1's pictures (18 of 53 snapshots and 4 of 10 records differed from HEAD's); pz_tvb stays unused, C6AAh lv_voffy's. Harness: tools/bstest/stepcheck.py --visit 2 (visit 2's render; a snapshot's $8050 >= 2), check_all.sh passes it for solve2 and fuzz2; docs/HARNESS.md. Tests: test_msxpuzl.py test_visit_2 and the command line with --visits 1,2, test_bstest.py test_stepcheck_visit_2. Results against HEAD 7c8635a's builds: in 20 option sets only BANK_PUZL and the new blob differ (romdiff --blocks PASS); regress.sh check against HEAD's records PASS (45 verdicts, 0 FAIL); Brainstorm's 20 traces 0 differ (solve2 728, fuzz2 606 frames); visit 1 byte-identical (53 snapshots in VRAM, registers, palette and RAM, 10 records in every part); visit 2's 66 stills on the MSX2, MSX2+, turbo R and at 50 Hz equal msxpuzl.py render --visit 2, its records clean, board 0 in visit 2's palette and boards 1-3 in visit 1's (quirk 5); visit 2's flow from power-on into the range and the title PASS on the Expert and the turbo R; BANK_PUZL 4,483 B free (4,590), every other bank as before; option sets 46 of 48 (DEMO_ACTORS 2/5 as before); make test: the 4 known failures only

change_details.after: Regenerator 2000 now indexes shared lexical-scope boundaries and performs monotonic block-range rendering while documenting the state and rendering invariants; upstream buildability remains established by the repository, not re-tested here.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Native Apple II collection; POM2 facade tests now exercise Apple //c and AppleMouse II firmware paths plus register, go and call control across game probes.
change_details.after: POM2 Games' native Apple II collection now records WARGALAGA II's 1.9 KiB memory recovery and Robot Space Station's tested DHGR-page code overlays; both remain named subjects within the collection.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Released Apple II and Commodore ports plus buildable/testable Commander X16 target; current main adds AI playtesting infrastructure with seven isolated platform stages and a broad set of gameplay-parity fixes, without tracker-side execution.
change_details.after: Moria8 adds disk save/load playtests, retry paths and deterministic failed-run capture across its 6502/65C02 ports; released/platform status is unchanged and tracker-side execution was not performed.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Starglider 2 remains byte-exact across 412,736 bytes; loop-wide sparse cells and canonical Dn pointer producers now survive only under proved write envelopes, while an A6 reader remains blocked at a cross-platform call predicate.
change_details.after: Starglider 2 remains byte-exact across 412,736 bytes while connected homing, HUD, collision-retirement and world-record recycling continuations gain original-CPU fixtures; global alias safety and complete gameplay remain unproved.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: v6.4.2 published; current devtools commit memory, graphics and assembler writes as one lease-bound machine change
change_details.after: konCePCja's KCPC debugger now publishes every frame through a documented shared-memory ring with sequence-numbered events and an independent fb_dump reader tested across Linux, macOS and Windows CI.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Firestaff's authenticated current-main startup matrix now passes four bounded real-media tests across all five games; Atari CSB rebirth/explosion rendering and executed-code CD-write tracing advanced, while Nexus playability and native display/input completeness remain open.
change_details.after: Firestaff now binds authenticated Atari ST Chaos Strikes Back archive members to the same original image and covers Atari ST 1.1 menu startup; broader native playability and Nexus completion remain open.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: current source marks v1.13 with hard-drive game-library and joystick-port configuration; Linux remains described as untested
change_details.after: ASE now emulates the Mega ST RP5C15 and IKBD clocks with emulated-time advancement and snapshot state; Linux remains described upstream as untested.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: active; Goblin, Speed Ski, Paratrooper and Things in the Dark source ports have deterministic upstream compile/runtime gates
change_details.after: Amy Studio adds ten explicitly labelled faithful COMPUTE! adaptations as ColecoVision examples, preserving source-game rules and quirks while remaining an original browser development environment.

events.title: Creation sheet: PNGs dropped on it, Add and Forget as cards, Modify on the sheet. The icon's poses stand on a dark grey ground and take a dropped PNG as the icon editor does (View.IconBox; takeIconPNG shared; the drop handlers belong to the page, newPage ends them; the editor sets its with each show), the portrait takes one as the sheet in play (ActPortrait while creating); the sheet draws itself anew (e.Act actRedraw). gpu.Drop carries the drop's screen pixel so the presenter picks the target by cell. The Add and Forget lists are cards of the portrait's head (a dropped PNG fitted) with the name and class beside it, laid out and paged by pickGrid (pickSaved, loadSaved; the bar's first word a parameter). Modify Character is the creation sheet on the member (editSheet, the loop shared with CreateCharacter; fresh keeps the items), Keep keeps the changes, Esc asks and puts the record back; the original's Raise/Lower bar and modifyDraw are gone. events.title: The analysis asks to correct the knowledge only for a refused seed in the program or an --entry outside it, as a routine outside the program can be code that the program copies there; a coverage gap is in-data only in a data range that the analyzer used; a second RTS dispatch through a recorded table gets its jump references, and a JMP run that overlaps an idiom is left out once

events.title: --fields finds a path through an empty list and names a cut list only when the fields show it; the listing and the source write a table entry with one function, so an RTS entry without a name is the address before its target in both; knowledge at reads the coverage of each map from one mask filled once, not from its range text at each address
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: assembler build --switch of main.asm writes the program also when the packed loader cannot be made, for a start screen of a captured stage, a segment below $0400 or a patch between the free ranges, and gives loader.written false with the reason; a missing Exomizer still refuses by name, and the loaded ranges and the start screen come from the same space as the switch defaults

events.title: Only a jump or call reference of the user or the LLM resolves a computed flow, and separate() and the export get the rule from one function: a JMP (N) reads its high byte in the same page, a vector is set by the code's own immediates only when no other write of the code changes it, and their values become reachable targets; an RTS or RTI after pushes is a flow too, with the target of two pushed immediates, else resolved by a jump reference of the idiom pass or the LLM; only a flow in code that a root reaches or that a run executed makes other code unknown; provenance separate lists each code region with reachable, executed and unknown, and the unresolved flows, so its --out file again holds every region, and a cut list of separate or leftovers names the --out file

change_details.after: Starglider 2 remains byte-exact across 412,736 bytes; loop-wide sparse cells and canonical Dn pointer producers now survive only under proved write envelopes, while an A6 reader remains blocked at a cross-platform call predicate.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.after: Attackwave m68k 2.4.7 now ships a VS Code extension and UAE-backed source debugger, exact 68000 cycle hints, Amiga custom-register diagnostics and decoded Copper views; CI builds tested VSIX packages for Linux x64, Windows x64 and macOS arm64.

change_details.after: Firestaff's authenticated current-main startup matrix now passes four bounded real-media tests across all five games; Atari CSB rebirth/explosion rendering and executed-code CD-write tracing advanced, while Nexus playability and native display/input completeness remain open.

events.title: renderer: 60+ fps fullscreen on the Win7 test machine, the picture unchanged pixel for pixel. The game draws straight into the window's frame (no copy of the screen a frame); wall faces are culled on the CPU by facing and frustum, in build order (sorting changes the soft edges' blends); a Fill of a whole image becomes the pass's clear; the sky and ground planes only test depth (beyond every face's depth, so writing it hid nothing, and the GPU now tests before it shades); gogpu's fullscreen flag is honoured on Windows; party cards cached per card. Battle view: -battle (POR_DEV=autocombat) has the computer fight both sides against eight monsters for measuring, the status line is drawn only when its text changes. Captures: the key script is paced by frames (deterministic frame for frame; ticks and frames interleaved differently each run), remaster ticks the view itself under a script, POR_FREEZE holds the frame for an outside grab, POR_OFFSCREEN forces the copy path, POR_SKIP leaves parts of the frame out (or undoes a saving) for timing and comparison; POR_QUIT runs play their keys too

events.title: The reverse-engineering skill names no file that a script owns: it puts the coverage of each recording into the knowledge, takes the default build and the not-executed count from the result of the generation, and keeps the project layout and the versions of one program in a reference file. The emulator skill drops its filler sections and gives the task to find the instruction that reads or writes an address. c64-basic gives machineCode with the addresses and the file offset of the bytes after the BASIC, and the disk, memory-map, packer and development skills give behaviour in place of mechanics, with the correct symbols file of a build
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: The analysis no longer drops a seed in silence: seeds gives the counts that the analyzer got, the counts over its limits, each seed that it did not decode with its reason (outside the program, in data, inside an instruction, into an instruction or data, past the end), and the data ranges that it left out for code. Each coverage gap has its reason, idioms.leftOut gives the idiom tables that another idiom already holds, and writtenNotExecuted lists the analyzer code on bytes that the runs wrote and never executed, with the instructions that reach it, as when an LLM routine led the decompiler into room data. The DXA regions are a list with --max-listed, the summary fields come first, and the skill gives each reason with its action and no longer explains the seeding

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: The Apple IIe/SoftCard environment now exposes kernel-managed W5100 socket and packetless TX/RX APIs, migrates Telnet to the kernel interface and adds a first working WGET client; network execution was not independently repeated.
change_details.after: Zapple-II / BP/M now includes a kernel-backed NETCCP remote-login server with Telnet option negotiation and terminal-independent command output; network execution remains upstream-reported.

before: CP/M Telnet and WGET client integration
after: CP/M Telnet and WGET client integration

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: BO5 is reported 100% for its bounded boss-overlay scope, while the in-tree PC runtime adds most stage overlays and fixes menu/prologue text; upstream explicitly says PC coverage is incomplete.
change_details.after: Castlevania Symphony of the Night decompilation has begun RBO6 boss-overlay asset/entity recovery and corrected Saturn stage-15 sprite/table typing; broader PC and overlay coverage remains incomplete.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Version 0.7.1 adds whole-game m68k-to-C translation roots and overlays, exact display-gap comparison, a web engine and an interrupt-aware Paula state model; upstream reports 2,376 tests, but the tracker did not run them.
change_details.after: amiga-re-kit 0.8.4 fixes long-run CIA timing, A500-style 24-bit/chip-RAM address decoding and CPU-versus-Copper register precedence from Alien Breed II full-game runs.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: v0.10.4 published; packaged demos now open from writable per-user copies, while Windows emulator integration remains explicitly experimental
change_details.after: PiST now analyzes TOS executables with persistent names/comments/code-data marks, live stopped-PC and Hatari coverage notes, picture inspection and source export admitted as a reconstruction only after vasm byte matching.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Primary source reviewed; independent build/run not performed
change_details.after: ND500X documents and indexes the ND-5000 '87 extension: 23 of 25 manual-labelled instructions are represented, with explicit implementation plans and unresolved RHOLE/AMODB scope.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Starglider 2 output remains byte-exact across 412,736 bytes while common airborne and ground launch-state contracts reduce unresolved record accesses from 219 to 207; broader semantics and minimum Amiga requirements remain open.
change_details.after: Starglider 2 remains byte-exact across 412,736 bytes; six connected disk/media helpers and two shared service-state fields now have bounded roles, while physical-media behavior and minimum Amiga requirements remain open.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Wizardry VII reconstruction now routes maze sounds through a recovered semantic C routine; the pinned README reports 271 of 1,099 routines in C (24.7%), with full C conversion still open.
change_details.after: Wizardry VII reconstruction adds named maze/region routines and derives typed data-file layouts from C declarations and recovered records; the pinned README still reports 271 of 1,099 routines in C (24.7%).

before: semantic C replacement under assembly comparison
after: semantic C replacement under assembly comparison

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Authenticated Nexus evidence now carries a retained retail BKR through Continue into a four-champion dungeon view, while FM Towns DM2 traces cover startup source frames; Firestaff-side Continue loading, HUD/viewport and presentation parity remain unimplemented or unverified.
change_details.after: Firestaff now hash-locks four authentic DM1 SNES cartridge images, decodes both H03 ROMDUNGEON slots and validates their shared 14-map structure; native SNES runtime, rendering, input and audio remain out of scope.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Primary source and build workflow reviewed; independent execution unverified
change_details.after: DCTelnet now builds with m68k-amigaos GCC 16.2, and its GCC binary restores cursor-key navigation in the shell and Mystic BBS by correcting signed CSI-byte handling.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Active Rust/C++ Amiga disk toolkit; decoded views now cover Workbench icons and indexed, EHB, HAM and 24-bit ILBM images with upstream corpus accounting and fuzz-bounded allocation checks.
change_details.after: Amiga Disk Engine now follows executable control flow into functions, cross-references and call graphs, names proven library calls, and exports source that GNU as rebuilds byte-for-byte across 39,363 corpus programs.

change_details.after: MAINL gains source-present DOS exception throw and global-unwind recovery covering 2,524 original bank bytes, but adds zero exact bytes; candidate size, EFLAGS and whole-TU gaps remain explicit.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Apple IIe 6502/Z80 SoftCard environment; current source fixes CP/M file truncation and directory search, caches terminal personality for faster output, and makes tab switching interrupt DIR/TYPE. Independent build/run not performed.
change_details.after: The Apple IIe/SoftCard environment now exposes kernel-managed W5100 socket and packetless TX/RX APIs, migrates Telnet to the kernel interface and adds a first working WGET client; network execution was not independently repeated.

after: CP/M Telnet and WGET client integration

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Dreamcast SH-4 decompilation now reports 98.3% of C-capable functions, 90.8% of eligible code bytes and 64.7% aggregate instruction coverage, with 57 functions left after seven newly proven functions and reader/repair fixes.
change_details.after: Dreamcast SH-4 decompilation now reports 99.5% of C-capable functions, 97.8% of eligible code bytes and 70.6% aggregate test coverage, with 18 of 3,299 C-capable functions and 17,086 eligible bytes left.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: ZX Spectrum disassembly now underpins v1.1.0 distribution builds for Aquarius+, Z88, Mitsubishi Multi 8, PC-8801 and SAM Coupé; tracker-side build/run not performed.
change_details.after: The shared Z80 reconstruction adds scenario disasters, square minimaps for PC-88 and Multi 8, and Aquarius+ 4bpp minimap plus text-layer menus, dialogs, budget and evaluation screens; Aquarius+ display details remain hardware-unverified.

before: shared simulation with platform-specific display, input, sound and file layers
after: shared simulation with platform-specific display, input, sound and file layers

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: PAL 2.00 PlayStation 2 matching reconstruction; the hero refactor types sound slots and draw queues and removes overlay-private hero structures, while matching and playability remain upstream work in progress.
change_details.after: PAL 2.00 PS2 reconstruction now shares typed LevelState/camera, render, pause, particle, puzzle and memory-card structures across overlays; these structural refactors do not by themselves establish additional matching or playability.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: The scoped DOS real-mode p-code view recovers 15 additional C decompilations across six builds (3,460/3,468 versus stock Ghidra's 3,445/3,468) and verifies a bounded renderer ownership block; whole-renderer and gameplay parity remain open.
change_details.after: Six-image DOS analysis now fixes the 55,015-byte save-slot layout, exercises caller/blitter contracts in 4,536 cases, and traces the default viewport split chain in 492 cases; runtime reachability, VGA output and whole-game parity remain open.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Source reviewed; upstream build and fidelity claims qualified
change_details.after: The reconstruction now records three passing Xtensa firmware profiles with exact size budgets and an original-ROM oracle with 14/14 scalar STRING cases observed twice; device execution and broad BASIC compatibility remain explicitly unverified.

after: three-profile Xtensa size and ABI verification

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Firestaff now rescans authenticated game data after folder access is granted or repaired, keeping launcher access ownership separate from the runtime; full campaign and presentation parity remain open.
change_details.after: Authenticated Nexus evidence now carries a retained retail BKR through Continue into a four-champion dungeon view, while FM Towns DM2 traces cover startup source frames; Firestaff-side Continue loading, HUD/viewport and presentation parity remain unimplemented or unverified.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: active; current main drives an Ameristar A2065 on physical Amiga 3000 hardware; no independent local build/run
change_details.after: AmiNetXDuo now pins reviewed NetX Duo TCP corrections for FIN acknowledgement, recovery boundaries/timers and DATA/FIN SACK recovery; the existing physical A3000/A2065 profile remains the only measured tracker runtime profile.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Early Amberstar reimplementation now integrates fight-or-flee choice, encounter triggering, battle outcomes, loot, defeated-monster removal and rescue/game-over handling; no complete-game claim.
change_details.after: Amberstar framework now loads English Amiga data, reproduces Amiga outro pictures/copper gradients and handles Amiga COSO/TFMX music and samples, including the seven-voice outro path; complete-game parity is not claimed.

events.title: Project metadata updated

after.name: Atari ST port
after.notes: Primary port documentation states that Hatari configured as an STE works, a plain ST also works, and at least 2 MB RAM is required. This is an upstream documented minimum, not tracker-side physical-hardware validation.

change_details.before: v1.22 game and Tools 1.19 published; development head adds AmbermoonImageEditor to the next cross-platform tool package
change_details.after: The Atari ST port now carries its unpacked original player/song data in-tree, no longer needs ORIGINAL at build time, and has accepted conversions for the documented Amiga song set through song 32; tracker-side build and listening tests were not performed.

before: native asset painting and palette editing
after: native asset painting and palette editing

Reader/repair tooling now handles dominator trees, shifted call indexes, call answers, hidden pointers with register arguments and frame words above stack copies.

change_details.after: Dreamcast SH-4 decompilation now reports 98.3% of C-capable functions, 90.8% of eligible code bytes and 64.7% aggregate instruction coverage, with 57 functions left after seven newly proven functions and reader/repair fixes.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Source reviewed; upstream build and fidelity claims qualified
change_details.after: The Amiga data set's entrance now follows Dungeon Master Amiga 3.6 timing: two-pixel door steps every 40 ms and a period-79 rattle every 0.8 s, with regression checks distinct from the Atari/CSBWin path.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Pharo-hosted Smalltalk-80 VM now implements and documents native primitive 103 text scanning with a guarded guest-code fallback; independent execution was not performed.
change_details.after: Pharo-hosted Smalltalk-80 VM corrects 32-bit positive-integer conversion between guest objects and the host, including little-endian LargePositiveInteger values up to four bytes; independent execution was not performed.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: In-progress PlayStation matching decompilation; current work deobfuscates collision triggers across all supported regional symbol maps without establishing a complete playable reconstruction.
change_details.after: In-progress PlayStation matching decompilation; current work deobfuscates shared character-collision structures and routines across bodyprog, player control, combat and multiple map actors without establishing complete playability.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Development head adds whole-machine SHA-256 state fingerprints, frame-boundary keyboard/joystick serialization, non-stalling plotter scheduling and configuration-relative RAM-disk backup handling.
change_details.after: Sharp MZ emulator/debugger now returns replay-seek run identifiers for reliable stop waits and hardens parallel testing so all built MZ-800/700/1500 binaries are exercised without oversubscribing shared MSYS Git/Bash resources.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Source reviewed; upstream build and fidelity claims qualified
change_details.after: The scoped DOS real-mode p-code view recovers 15 additional C decompilations across six builds (3,460/3,468 versus stock Ghidra's 3,445/3,468) and verifies a bounded renderer ownership block; whole-renderer and gameplay parity remain open.

change_details.before: Source reviewed; upstream build and fidelity claims qualified

change_details.after: Multi-format Acorn disk editor now detects and refuses Acorn Z80 CP/M images whose locked $.CPMDISC catalogue placeholder masks the CP/M filesystem, directing those images to CP/M Disk Wrangler to prevent destructive DFS writes.

events.title: Level 2's step 13: level 2's play field. tools/mkrom.py: level 2's BOBHASH takes its own play-field frames (sprites_l2.json "field": ids D0h + their index, types 2, 14 and 16 with their hit flash's silhouette, the suspect's white blink), its atlas at L2_ATLAS cut into two banks with a table each (atlas_banks: the count's bit 7 when another bank follows; one bank kept byte for byte, level 1's), gen/field_l2.inc (level 2's field tables with their names suffixed; its dynamic frames' tables checked to be level 1's), the vats' display tables in L2_TAB at L2_VATS 9700h (tools/mapcells.py vat_tables: per map row the vats over it, per vat its columns, rows and first vat_shown index, the 48 T words' tiles) and gen/vats_l2.inc (vat_shown's start, each column's static look), the descriptors' new fields lv_dynp (the dynamic slot's page: 3, level 2's 2 at line 224), lv_tcn (the tile cache's slots, negated: 256, 224) and lv_fld (the level's field tables in BANK_FIELD), with VRAM checks (the atlas, the slot and the tile slots apart). msx/field.asm: fld_l1 and fld_l2 (FIELD_LATE, FIELD_DYN0/1, field_tab, field_look) copied by fb_init to fb_flate ... fb_flook and read there (the trolley in fb_late's group with level 2's lift), the dynamic slot's copies from (lv_dyn, lv_dynp), field_upload bank by bank, and a piece's copy onto the page shown in all its parts in a row (fb_cmd2 at EDC0h holds three: the V9958 ring crossed at x 256 and y 256 took two blanks, the trolleys' top lines a picture ahead, 9-23 pictures a ride on the MSX2+ and the turbo R). msx/isr.asm: isr_fbgo and ifg_fin start the chain's parts each when the one before is done (fb_cp, fb_cn); publish counts the picture (fb_tick) before the interrupts may take the list, rc2.asm do_publish no longer after it (a list the split's uploads readied and the VBLANK took in between went on screen without its play-field BOBs: a lift missing for 6 pictures). msx/tiles.asm tc_load and msx/cold.asm tiles_init: the level's slots (lv_tcn). msx/level2.asm l2_init: a fresh level 2 sets vat_shown (vat_sh0), vat_disp and vat_chg (0). Harness: tools/bstest/fieldcheck.py --level 2 (level 2's frames as its ROM uploads them; hostage-like BOBs torn per object), tools/msxframe.py (FieldLooks; the tile area per level: cache slots against TC_TILE, the atlas's frames; --field: patches and the list's BOBs in the expected picture), tools/bstest/hz.tcl hz_l2_field_jobs and hz_l2_still_jobs' drive; tests (test_level2_rom.py: l2_hash, atlas_banks, field_inc, vat_tables; test_bstest.py: the tear per object; test_msxsprites.py: FieldLooks); docs/HARNESS.md 5.22, docs/MSX_ARCHITECTURE.md. Results: level 2's 20 traces 0 differ, lost counters 0; the field check over tour's windows (the start, types 14 and 16, the four trolley rides, the drips, the arrest) and barrel's stairs on the MSX2, the MSX2+ and the turbo R: 0 differ on the product-caps build, and on the trace build but the drive's teleport sweep (fx), one picture of a staged 2-piece item (tr) and 5 pixels of a trolley entering a picture early (tr); the field lists against the bench's calls 5,467 BOBs exact; 36 stills with the play field exact, the tile area clean; the trolley, the suspect (and its blink), type 14 and type 16's body whole in the play field; option sets 46 of 48; the fixed area 298 B free in the product (315), 163 at the lowest (180), FIELD 1,183 / 1,142 (EXTJOY), FRONT 1,897, BANK_L2 1,445; make test: the 4 known failures only

events.title: Level 2's step 12: the global sprite pool in the ROM. tools/mkrom.py takes tools/msxsprites.py --pool's files (build/msx/sprites.*; the Makefile: bobcatalog.py level2 in make sprites, the pool run in make msx after level 2's palette): sprites.bin at SPR_BASE_BANK (27 banks, level 1's 23: every later block 4 banks on, once; 123 of 128 banks, 1 MiB), FIELD_ID0 D0h, each level's BOBHASH (level 1's from sprites_l1.json: its 190 sprite entries unchanged, its 40 play-field ids +8; level 2's: its own sprite frames and ids, type 1's two torso frames as BOB_HIDDEN FEh, and level 1's 26 play-field frames it shares with level 1's ids, its own play-field frames still off until step 13), level 2's atlas placed at L2_ATLAS (2 banks, not used yet), the descriptors' new fields lv_sidx and lv_spark (SPR_BOB_INDEX_Ln, SPR_SPARK_Ln - 1: msx/msx.inc LV_SIZE 27, sprites.asm os_new, player.asm's hit spark), and a BOBHASH slot's last byte: the lines a frame's picture reaches above its draw call's place (pool_above, from the records' patterns: 20-21 for type 1's 16 joint compositions, 0 for every other frame; level 1's checked to be 0). msx/bob.asm bf_vis takes a record as shown while that picture, those lines higher and 2 pixels wider, is in the play area; bfs_new keeps the lines in O_TOPU, sprites.asm pend_build in V_TOPU and sb_object parks an object once its first line with pixels is below the play area (type 1 vanished up to 21 lines early); bf_fq gives a BOB_HIDDEN frame no object. msx/level2obj.asm l2_flash: the muzzle flash of types 1, 2 and 16, drawn before their other parts, under an owner of its own (as RoboCop's flash), so that the legs keep their part and their object (one picture of the flash's frame at the legs' place, or none, on each shot before). Harness: tools/bstest/romdiff.py --blocks (each block of gen/banks.inc at its own bank; --allow), relocheck.py (bank pairs OLD:NEW or a name; one-byte operands NAME + k of changed byte equates, a moved label's byte after an imm8 instruction), objcmp.py (--sprites, the joints' picture box, the hidden frames, --procs, --rows), hz.tcl hz_l2_objs_jobs (4.2 check 3), l2base.py fresh: the game's VRAM at tick 300 may hold each sprite set's entries in another order (the same entries; the order is the BOB runs' timing, checked by the LOCKSTEP records); docs/HARNESS.md 5.15, 5.21, 5.22, docs/MSX_ARCHITECTURE.md. Results: base -> the relocation layer (mkrom and the descriptor only): every data block byte-identical at its new bank but the pool, LEVEL_BANK and L2_TAB (romdiff: PASS; LEVEL_BANK's BOBHASH 190 entries identical, 40 ids +8), the code banks only relocated words and bank operands but FRONT's grown descriptors (checked field by field) and their `ld hl,lv_desc - LV_SIZE` (prod, ext, l2); level 2's 20 traces 0 differ in all 1,022 fields and in the 112 bullet and explosion fields, lost counters 0; 4.2 check 3 (bench draw_bob calls against rc2_objs_rom, t1left, barrel, drone, tour, end on the MSX2, the MSX2+ and the turbo R): types 1, 5, 6, 49 exact but the budget's left-outs (ENEMY_CAP=0 build), loading lags of the same BOB and ticks held while the view moves, no extra, no frame missing from the table; their stills' sprite pixels exact (the rest msxframe's object order and the V9938's right border); level 1, Brainstorm, the range and the title as the base (l2base: PASS, 227 jobs); 46 of 48 option sets, the fixed area 315 B free in the product (380 before), 180 at the lowest (DIAG + PZ_TEST), FRONT -6, BANK_L2 1,569; make test: the 4 known failures only

events.title: Level 2's step 9: the new object types. msx/level2obj.asm ports the seven types only level 2 has, routine by routine: type 1 ($C736: the step counter, obj_fall at y + 2Ch, walk_d6, a copy of obj_walk that returns $EF42's D6, on 4 frames in 64 a bullet and the muzzle flash, facing right type 6 in direction 4, facing left the original's leftover type D6 in direction 10h (0: the slot written, no bullet; Q2), the legs by the facing before the step, the torso by the facing after it); type 2 ($C868 and the arrest tail $C91A: the message every 64 frames, x held at 180h, ac_camdx 500h, from count 46h the shooting pose and on count & 33h = 0 the flash and a type-5 bullet with accelerations -2000h / -1000h (+3000h when count & 40h), the white blink on bit 3, the hit points back to 4, touched: "ARREST SUCESSFUL.", sound 21h, $16D0, $16C4 = 40h); type 5 ($D0E2: grow, fall until a solid cell 18h below or RoboCop's touch, which also costs 0Ah x DAMAGE_X, the splash); type 6 ($D1E2 with $D1CA, $D1D0, $D1DE: the launch window y 1A0h-1D0h, barrel_gap, the bounce speed -7.0 / -4.5, the roll and bounce, byte 2 = the draw's D0 low byte, $16BA's when not drawn) and its death $C33E ($15F2, a pickup every 4th kill, 1Ch at the 16th; the explosion is type 0 because $C35A clears D5, and after a pickup it comes at y 0: step 1's note on the type was wrong, the ledger corrected); type 14 ($CE0A: faces RoboCop, the smoke (explosion 1) and a lobbed grenade on 2 frames in 64); type 16 ($CD7A: walker1's legs, fires at counts 20h and 28h, wraps at 2Eh, the body aiming from 14h); type 49 ($E6C0 and the flight $E728: half steps through fly_half, which keeps the original's ext.l / swap / asr.l #1, so a negative step moves a little less than half, the turn towards aim_at's target, its touch 18h at most twice as a missile, the explosion when touched or its life runs out). lv_noten stays level2.asm's (only 45 not counted, default 25). tools/bstest/l2stub.py's table is empty now (every level-2 routine ported) and tests/test_level2_rom.py checks the handlers' addresses against the type records itself; docs/HARNESS.md 5.22 and docs/AMIGA_ANALYSIS.md (type 6's death, the homing flight). Level 2's 20 traces on top of step 8 equal the plain references in all 1,022 fields over every row (end 259, barrel 901, t1left 341, drone 401, tour 2,654 on the MSX2, the MSX2+ and the turbo R, cont to its game over), and the enemy bullets' and explosions' slots outside the field set too (112 scratch fields, 0 differ); on top of step 7 the same against the references with step 8's routines stubbed; level 1, Brainstorm, the range and the title as the base (l2base: PASS, 227 jobs; the code banks but BANK_L2 byte-identical to step 7's and step 8's builds); BANK_L2 1,587 B free (6,605 used), the fixed area unchanged (380, lowest 245); 46 of 48 option sets as before; make test: the 4 known failures only

events.title: Level 2's step 5: the logic's level constants, level 1 only. Every level bank starts with the same level header (objects.asm lv_htab ... LV_HDR_END A0F0h: the handler table, lv_init, lv_tick, lv_hz, then lv_swn1, lv_swlast, lv_hzxn/yn, lv_hzxm/ym/all and lv_noten, level1.asm's values held to the equates by ds lines) and holds msx/lvshared.asm right after it: sw_ptr (40 entries), the spawn walk's shortcuts with 5-byte masks (SW_MAX 40, SW_MB 5) and the handlers levels 1 and 2 share (t3, t4, t12, t13, t15, t30, t31, t45 and t_xy ... t_word), moved verbatim out of level1.asm; tools/mkrom.py writes level 2's copy gen/lvshared_l2.asm (its labels and the level data's names suffixed _l2) and checks after the assembly that every copy's labels equal level 1's, so objects.asm and special.asm call the shared code at level 1's addresses whatever level bank is mapped (a dry run of a level-2 bank: 44 labels at level 1's addresses, 19 data operands apart); objects.asm reads uf_last's values from the header and calls lv_noten (not_enemy gone: LC1 53 B free, 39 at the base); special.asm reads the hazards' cells and masks from the header, sets vat_cut_line to CAh every tick ($9150) and sends handler 4 to the sp_trolley stub; mapobj.asm's ao_acts entry 3 is act_0c, a label on ao_look; msx.inc repacks the shortcuts' caches and gives every level-2 home of the plan's 3.4 (barrel_gap, vat_phase, vat_shown, vat_disp, vat_chg, vat_cut_line, pz_tvb, fo_cont); tools/cellmasks.py writes 5-byte masks, no sw_ptr, and other levels' names suffixed. Level 1's traces 0 differ (cov1, cov0, cov0_tr, die, over, end), the product configuration's traces equal the base's, LOCKSTEP records 0 differ, the start checks 0, the stills identical; the relocation drive (build/emu/drive_reloc, documented in docs/HARNESS.md) equal to the base's

last_commit.message: NFS_DOS.EXE of EA's 1997 CD accepted too (a player's: "not the version ReNFS knows"). Its build, dated 17 June 1996, the same 1,254,591 bytes, differs from the 19 June one laid out and relocated only in the give-up branch of keys_control_word 0x48bec (the word written 0x000087a0, not 0xffff87a0; the function 4 bytes longer) and one German text at 0xe3814, neither read by the port: exe.c takes either FNV-1a (0x76078ed2, 0x21ef7c33). With every read checked against those bytes, the 1997 CD drew the same pictures in the front end, the four replays (equal at every snapshot) and nine races. Our CD copy has three bits flipped where the 1997 CD's bytes match their neighbours (NOTES §1). The message no longer says 1996.

change_details.before: Working Win32 reconstruction and SDL2 port; upstream reports 516,228 of 518,656 strict-matching bytes (99.5319%) with 2,428 differing positions in 565 runs, while current navigation/expression probes remain deliberately unretained.
change_details.after: Working Win32 reconstruction and SDL2 port; upstream now reports 517,025 of 518,656 strict-matching bytes (99.6855%), leaving 1,631 differences in 264 runs while all 1,539 mapped functions retain their addresses.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Systemless 0.100.0 extends its classic-Mac PowerPC runtime with CFBundle/CFURL FSRef conversion, native fixed-function OpenGL 1.2 presentation and additional CoreFoundation getters; established Warcraft II playability remains an upstream claim.
change_details.after: Systemless 0.100.0 remains the published baseline; development head now implements QuickDraw AngleFromSlope for PowerPC applications with signed fixed-point edge-case tests through the PEF import path.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Incremental DOS C reconstruction still reports 286 strict routines among 331 identities; its native boundary audit now requires exact intermediate FLAGS witnesses and independently rejects a wrong-CS and ADD-assignment mutant without establishing whole-game completion.
change_details.after: Incremental DOS C reconstruction still reports 286 strict routines among 331 identities; current native fixtures record DOSBox-X executable provenance for bounded 128-case RES03F1/RES0464 comparisons without adding recovery credit.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Source reviewed; upstream build claims qualified in notes
change_details.after: Byte-exact Amiga disassembly/rebuild plus enhanced branch; upstream now reports WinUAE tests for the corkscrew scroller, 48 KiB mirror cache and 50 Hz presentation, while real-hardware validation remains open.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Starglider 2's generated catalogue now projects 2,741 native app references with explicit base provenance while preserving byte-identical C/vasm output and all 57 assets; byte ownership and remaining semantics are unchanged.
change_details.after: Starglider 2 output remains byte-exact while a canonical common-prefix join restores six typed XYZ projections, reducing unresolved record accesses from 277 to 271; broader semantics remain incomplete.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Substantial desktop Sega machine/peripheral emulator; Windows package is described upstream as ready to run, with fidelity unverified here.
change_details.after: Desktop SG-1000/SC-3000/SF-7000 and related emulator/debugger; MSX1 support now includes two joysticks, logical cartridge breakpoints and ASCII 16 MegaROM banking while other MegaROM mappers remain unsupported.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Source inspected; no independent build or execution
change_details.after: USA PlayStation matching reconstruction; stage data now delegates per-area map, image, music and object rows to room instances while upstream reports a clean matching build.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Development head now decodes native DM1 FM Towns GRAPHICS.DAT RLE assets and verifies shipped 320×200 asset output plus authenticated DM2 Towns HUD portraits; broader cross-game presentation and gameplay parity remain open.
change_details.after: Firestaff v3.0.416 and current head add bounded authenticated launcher, Theron and cross-platform startup evidence while explicitly limiting picker coverage to available media and leaving full campaign/display parity open.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: v2.3.0 published with reconstructed dform plus DOS-derived dcopy/dcomp utilities; independent rebuild and runtime verification remain unperformed

events.title: A room's, an actor's and the stage's generated C is one include per run, not one per module with ROOM_PART selecting a part: a run is a module's objects that follow each other in a unit with nothing else between them, written as <module>.inc, or <module>_1.inc, <module>_2.inc in address order where other data or a unit boundary interrupts the module, and the declarations as declarations.inc, or declarations_<unit>.inc per unit; the build generates the runs the overlay's sources include, so a source naming a run that is not there fails it. The 75 ROOM_PART selectors in 23 rooms' and the stage's sources are the runs they selected. The area objects' place lists are a module of their own (object_places) beside the object table (objects), so the stage's objects are object_places_1, objects and object_places_2. sync-c writes the runs, finds a stage's source (src/stages/<stage>/stage.c) and a room's units by their declarations include (it missed the MIST rooms, under mist_<room>/). events.title: The Akropolis stage overlay and its map pages live with the stage: map_akropolis is the package akropolis_stage, its source src/stages/akropolis/stage.c and its header include/stages/akropolis/stage.h; the map pages mappic_s1_00 and mappic_s1_02 are akropolis_map and akropolis_helicopter_landing_pad_map, their sources src/stages/akropolis/map/akropolis.c and helicopter_landing_pad.c and their declarations include/stages/akropolis/map.h (out of the shared include/mappic/mappic.h). The manifest entries name their sources (src), and a data-only unit of such an entry gets a zero-length variantsrc text run where its data begins, so its .data takes that sibling's source (gen_overlay_configs.py). The disc tree names the stage's four map files akropolis_map_page_0 to _3 (30100-30103). Every reference follows: the symbol maps (renamed), checksums, imports, the room tools' stage table, the usage, observation, residency and note tables (the seven retired shape records' notes now name the shape models), and the documentation. NAMING.md: an overlay of one unit may be a loose file. A clean build matches

events.title: The Akropolis map is assets: its two pages are packages of the group rooms/akropolis/map (page_1, mappic_s1_00, which map files 30100 and 30101 load; page_2, mappic_s1_02, file 30102), loaded into the PE slot, whose 16 room shapes are declared untextured models with bindings, placed whole and exported under their C symbols. The stage overlay binds both pages, and its shape table names each shape through the page its row names (package.map_page_file_id: 30000 + 100 x stage + page), as map_page_1.square and so on, which its C writes as &gMappicS100SquareShape (was (void*)0x8012EFD8); the pages' C includes the generated models (with their footprint comments). The pages' 32 model objects leave overlays.toml and the stage map's 16 owner= lines its symbol map; the legacy records of the two packages and of the seven shapes only they held leave asset_data.py (ratchet 4833 ASSETS, 580 EMBEDDED_ASSETS). The other map pages' raw shape includes are named by order among the versions of each shared stream, so with page 1's versions gone six of their names changed, which six page sources follow (mappic_s2_00, s2_02, s3_00, s3_02, s4_00, s4_02). package.file_ids lists every file holding a package. A clean build matches

events.title: The Akropolis stage's packages declare their models and collision only as assets: overlays.toml loses the 460 model, model source, animation, collision grid, header and patch objects of the 68 entries for its rooms, the MIST's and every package they bind (with those entries' other packages, which share their objects), and the build takes them from the packages' declarations instead. Every model there is a declared model, and the 115 copies no package placed yet are placed now (arrays to TmdSource record); the 25 grids beside the square's are collision assets placed by their rooms, each with its cell_face_list_macro (the square's too), and No. 9's and the lesser Stranger's patches are collision assets with their pieces. package.placed_models and placed_collisions list what packages place as the build's rows, and gen_overlay_configs' declared_models, declared_collisions and declared_collision_patches add them to the manifest's (which still wins where it declares an object); the room tools take a grid's face-list binding from its asset, and the build checks a grid's placement ends where its header begins. Every animation run there was a declared clip already. Generated includes and splat configs are byte-identical

events.title: Code references between stage-1 packages are exports too: the shooting gallery (29: its functions Pierce calls, its task tables, the targets' models), the plaza (35 police clips), the cafeteria (its scene tasks), the cafeteria Stranger (5 clips the boss plays), the MIST parking, the square, the landing pad (No. 9's spark line and vibration) and the fire escape (the lesser Stranger's collision grid) export 78 names, and the 9 actors naming them require those packages. A package's link takes every export of the packages it binds or requires (package.link_symbols; where two give one symbol different addresses, the one its data names), written by gen_overlay_configs.py as absolute symbols into the overlay's generated symbol map, so splat names them in its output and the link imports them; ninja_config writes no export files of its own. tools/check/check_exports.py, run by the unscoped build, holds each of the 216 exports to its own package's linked image (defined there, at its slot address plus at). The banks' borrows field is gone: a bank binds clips from the packages its package binds or requires, which now covers the police and the cafeteria boss. The 79 absolute lines the exports replace leave the 9 actor maps. The sucklerceph packages' references into Shelter rooms stay, waiting on imports

events.title: Stage 1's last player clip tables in C are animation banks: the cafeteria's opening and follow-up, the landing pad's departure and the sanctuary's player scene are declared (bank, schema and placement, 4 of each), and the MIST parking's conversation and shop banks, declared already, replace their C copies; each room includes its generated table. A placed bank binds clips from the packages its package binds or requires (animation.declared.bank_place), and its C names such a clip by that package's export at its address (gen_animation_source.clip_symbol): the anmc woman, the cafeteria Stranger and Rupert, the departure and the sanctuary Rupert export the 14 clips those banks bind, and the 14 owner= lines naming them leave the room maps. The build's export symbols include what a package's banks bind (package.bank_exports). The stage-1 room maps keep two owner= lines, the square's post-cutscene area updates, which the shared cutscene task names in the fire escape and the parking only for a branch that runs in the square

events.title: The Akropolis stage overlay is a package: it loads into the stage slot, requires gameplay and exports the 63 placement tables its rooms' area variants point to (patio_variant_1_placements, ...). The rooms' data names them as rooms/akropolis/stage.<export>, through the stage they require, and their C writes the array bare (gMapAkropolisPatioVariant1Placements, was (void*)&gMapAkropolisPatioVariant1Placements). Decoding names a pointer into a required package by its exports (package.required_exports), and a room of a stage that is a package no longer reads the stage's own names from its symbol map, only the lines that map gives for the room itself; the decoded rooms are unchanged but for those 63 references. The build's export symbols cover required packages as well as bindings, and the 63 owner=map_akropolis lines leave the room maps, with the fountain's stale gActor101100Tasks (it binds the recolored brute, whose table is gActor01100Tasks)

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Region-pinned extraction, assembly rebuild and per-function C equivalence/matching workflow. Game-derived source generated locally; matching whole executable with ASM fallback is not complete C recovery. Test equivalence is scoped to supplied cases and excludes selected SR flags.
change_details.after: Dreamcast SH-4 decompilation with region-pinned rebuild and function-equivalence workflow; upstream reports 60.1% of C-capable functions and 23.3% of eligible code bytes complete, with 13.2% aggregate instruction coverage

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Portable Z80 assembly OS with kernel, drivers, filesystem, target configurations and SDK examples; native source development rather than binary reconstruction.
change_details.after: Portable native Z80 assembly OS with documented CMake/z88dk builds; generated libraries now use deterministic archive metadata

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.after: Dreamcast SH-4 decompilation with disc-driven reconstruction and C-equivalence workflow; upstream reports 93.9% of C-capable functions and 66.4% of eligible code bytes complete, with 45.9% aggregate instruction coverage

change_details.before: Source inspected; no independent build or execution

change_details.after: Starglider 2's generated catalogue now projects 2,741 native app references with explicit base provenance while preserving byte-identical C/vasm output and all 57 assets; byte ownership and remaining semantics are unchanged.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Development head extends 65C816 recovery through pointer-built JMP/JML dispatch, nested-table cuts and BEQ-guarded nonzero indices, with bounded real-ROM gains and remaining structural over-reads documented.
change_details.after: Development head now recognizes NES inline dispatchers that save Y in absolute RAM and narrows conditional tail calls to genuine entries; bounded Punch-Out!! and SMB3 corpus results improve without treating ROM writes as harmless save noise.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Development head verifies mixed-media DM1 AUTO selection from the no-game launcher through FM Towns and PC media handoff, alongside new Theron SDL input and Saturn BKR evidence; complete cross-game parity remains open.
change_details.after: Development head now decodes native DM1 FM Towns GRAPHICS.DAT RLE assets and verifies shipped 320×200 asset output plus authenticated DM2 Towns HUD portraits; broader cross-game presentation and gameplay parity remain open.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Source inspected; current upstream adds StuffIt 1.5 HMF-entry extraction and headerless LZC/LZW handling with tests, without an independent tracker build or execution
change_details.after: CiderPress II now implements streaming PackIt/StuffIt method-3 Huffman compression intended to match StuffIt 1.5, extending the already reviewed vintage-Mac archive extraction path; independently unbuilt and unrun.

events.title: Stage 1's rooms are packages, and every actor they spawn is named through a binding: the other 20 rooms load into the room slot and require gameplay and the Akropolis stage overlay; 17 of them bind the packages their resources spawn (71 bindings with the square's), and 50 more packages export the task tables those name, by the names the room links already used (61 tables in 51 packages; the rat and moth, the officers, the departure, the security monitors and the three sucklerceph and skull stalker packages export one per role). All 95 resource entries that point outside their room now name <binding>.<export> instead of an address (the square's grinning_stranger.task_desc is grinning_stranger.tasks, like the rest); six whose own file is a texture or not on the disc spawn from a package another entry loads, and resolve to the one export of any binding at that address. The build writes build/exports/<room>.txt, each export a room's data references at its package's slot address, and adds it to that room's undefined symbols (a split input); a symbol two bindings give different addresses is an error. package.slot_of finds an actor package in a variant entry's slots too

events.title: A replay of a rebuild with a loader starts the rebuild in the phase of the original at the entry: the replay core holds the rebuild on its first fetch at the entry until the raster beam is where the original had it, and gives it the CIA timers and the interrupt state of the original there (c64run protocol 7, align), as that phase depends on how the original started and a loader can only set the one of the capture; a program that starts its CIA timers without a force load, as Barbarian does, no longer drifts to a false FAIL

events.title: The knowledge keeps the coverage of each map by its project path, as one coverage.jsonl line of ranges for each map and access kind, and the coverage of a space is the union of its maps: a new map of a path replaces the earlier map of that path, so a recording made again into the same folder no longer leaves the code of the old session as executed; coverage gives imported, replaced, known, added and removed, and a coverage.jsonl of an earlier version is refused with the remedy to delete it and import the maps again
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: A deleted or changed file that the knowledge gives as evidence shows at the point of use: docs link lists in evidence each such file with its state and the revisions that give it, by the latest SHA-256 of the file in the knowledge, without a FAIL, and record --out lists each file of the folder that the knowledge gives as evidence and that the record changed, with the hint to import the new coverage.bin, which replaces the map of the earlier recording

events.title: I fixed the MZ-800 state right after a reset. The emulator put the GDG into MZ-700 mode (DMD 08h) and did not map VRAM at 8000h. On the real machine, after power on and after RESET the GDG is in MZ-800 mode (DMD 0, 320x200) and the memory map is the same as after OUT E4h: ROM at 0000h, CG-ROM at 1000h, VRAM at 8000h-9FFFh, ROM at E000h, RAM elsewhere. MZ-700 mode is switched on later by the ROM (OUT CEh with 08h at E816h). This is shown in the MZ-800 Service Manual (pages 6 and 7), and a simulation of the GDG gate-level netlist gives the same map after a cold and a warm reset.

The flames draw named cells of the landing pad's sparks page, now declared: flame_*, tongue_*, burning_* and smudge_* (30 cells), with 21 palettes the extractor called unread - smudge on row 270 and the twenty fire palettes on row 271 the tongues and burning flames step through - as its variants; the effect tasks are named for their effects (GolemFlameTask, FlameTongueTask, FlameSpriteTask, GunfireParticleTask, MuzzleFlashTask, ExplosionFireballTask, ImpactBurstTask; were ..Task45, ..4C, ..52, ..59, ..44, ..184, ..185), effect 0x4C is EFFECT_NO9_FLAME_TONGUE, and the gunfire smudge is documented as subtractive (was 'additive'). change_details.before: Primary source reviewed; independent build/run not performed
change_details.after: Apple IIe 6502/Z80 SoftCard environment; current source fixes CP/M file truncation and directory search, caches terminal personality for faster output, and makes tab switching interrupt DIR/TYPE. Independent build/run not performed.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: working Win32 reconstruction and SDL2 port; the inflight-computer layout now matches 1,035 of 1,040 bytes with all 52 relocation operands at original offsets, while residual stack-offset bytes, whole-file identity and gameplay completeness remain incomplete
change_details.after: Working Win32 reconstruction and SDL2 port; upstream reports 516,228 of 518,656 strict-matching bytes (99.5319%) with 2,428 differing positions in 565 runs, while current navigation/expression probes remain deliberately unretained.

events.title: Project metadata updated

after.name: Tang Nano 20K SMD variant
after.notes: Upstream's measured fast20 configuration with SMD and tape reader uses 89% logic and 45 of 46 BSRAM blocks, routes successfully, and boots SINTRAN from 21540& in 26 seconds. This is a verified board/build combination, not a minimum FPGA or memory requirement.

evidence.excerpt: SMD + tape reader ... routed; 21540& boots SINTRAN in 26 s

after.name: Tang Nano 20K Winchester default
after.notes: Upstream reports the default Winchester plus tape-reader build at 87% logic and 45 of 46 BSRAM blocks, routed and booting SINTRAN from 20500&. SMD and Winchester together do not route on the tested Tang configuration.

evidence.excerpt: Winchester + tape reader (the default) ... routed; 20500& boots SINTRAN

change_details.before: Primary source reviewed; independent build/run not performed
change_details.after: Reconstructed ND-120 Verilog system with measured FPGA bring-up: tested Tang Nano 20K SMD-only and Winchester variants boot SINTRAN, while combined SMD+Winchester routing fails on Tang; Nexys and MEGA65 work continue.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Active multi-platform decompilation: current CI builds the PlayStation variants, Linux ports and a native Sega Saturn SH-2 image; runtime/playability not independently tested
change_details.after: Matching Mega Man X4 decompilation: the same C source builds byte-matching US, JP and EU PlayStation executables, native Linux ports, and a non-matching Sega Saturn build. Runtime/playability not independently tested.

change_details.after: Starglider 2 semantic restoration preserves complete C/vasm byte equality for the mapped output and reduces unclassified bytes from 25,585 to 22,445; substantial function and field meaning remains unresolved.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.after: Active incomplete browser remake; current work adds measured cross-backend villager load and grip checks and fixes a truncated WebGPU regression signature. The tracker did not run the browser build.
